questionText:
Other things remaining the same, an increase in the tax rate on corporate
profits will:

options.text: have no impact on the cost of debt

solution.quick: An increase in corporate profit tax rates enhances the interest tax shield, making debt relatively cheaper compared to equity.
solution.concept:
According to NCERT Class 12 Business Studies Part 2, Chapter 9: Financial Management, Section 9.5: Factors affecting Capital Structure (Tax Rate):
'Interest paid on debt is a tax-deductible expense, whereas dividends on equity are paid out of after-tax profits. A higher tax rate lowers the after-tax cost of debt [Kd = Interest * (1 - Tax Rate)], making debt relatively cheaper.'
solution.step_by_step:
1. Analyze the relationship between corporate tax rate and cost of debt.
2. Interest payments reduce taxable income, saving taxes equal to (Interest * Tax Rate).
3. When the tax rate increases, the tax shield grows larger, reducing the net post-tax cost of debt.
4. Equity receives no such tax relief.
5. Therefore, higher corporate taxes make debt relatively cheaper.
6. Matches Option A.
